questions.stem: Which of the following processes moves molecules across a cell membrane against their concentration gradient?
questions.explanation: Active transport uses energy, usually from ATP, to move molecules from a region of lower concentration to one of higher concentration. The other three are passive and move molecules down their gradient.

rationales.A: Simple diffusion is passive and moves molecules down their gradient.
rationales.B: Facilitated diffusion uses carrier or channel proteins but is still passive.
rationales.D: Osmosis is the passive movement of water across a membrane.

questions.stem: Which TWO of the following are components of the fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane?
questions.explanation: The fluid mosaic model describes a phospholipid bilayer in which proteins are embedded or attached, free to move laterally. Cellulose and peptidoglycan belong to cell walls, not membranes, and cholesterol is interspersed, not a sheet.

questions.stem: A red blood cell is placed in a hypertonic solution. What is MOST likely to happen?
options: It shrinks as water leaves the cell.
questions.explanation: In a hypertonic solution the external solute concentration is higher, so water moves out of the cell by osmosis and the cell crenates.
